title: The senses, the mind and lasting peace

verses.sa: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
verses.tr: As the winds carry a boat on water, even one roaming sense can sweep away the mind's discernment.
verses.angle: vayu, the force that carries the boat off course
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna warns that a single sense can drag the whole mind off course. Listen for the exact force that sweeps away judgment.

body.text: As the winds carry a boat on water, even one roaming sense can sweep away the mind's discernment. The word vayu is the force that carries the boat off course, and Krishna uses that exact image to show how one sense can sweep away discernment. Krishna now turns to the one who controls the senses and finds a steady wisdom.

verses.sa: तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
verses.tr: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the wisdom of one whose senses are fully restrained from sense-objects is steady.
verses.angle: Mahabaho: the mighty-armed strength to restrain the senses
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just warned that a single wandering sense can sweep away the mind's discernment. Now he states the result of true inner mastery.

body.text: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, the wisdom of one whose senses are fully restrained from sense-objects is steady. Krishna calls Arjuna mighty-armed, reminding him that the strength to control the senses already lies within him. Once the senses are fully restrained in every way, wisdom stands firm and steady. Krishna then contrasts the inner state of the self-controlled with the ordinary waking and sleeping of the world.

verses.sa: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
verses.tr: What is night for all beings is wakefulness for the self-controlled one. What all beings wake toward is night for the seer who knows the real.
verses.angle: the sage's night is the world's day
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna carries on the idea of the steady mind, and now he tells Arjuna about the inner clock of the sage.

body.text: What is night for all beings is wakefulness for the self-controlled one. What all beings wake toward is night for the seer who knows the real. The sage's day is the world's night. Where everyone else wakes up to chase things, the seer is awake in what is night for all beings, and what all beings wake toward is night for the seer. Krishna says that just as rivers pour into the sea, desires flow into a steady person without stirring their peace.

verses.sa: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठंसमुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वेस शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥
verses.tr: As rivers flow into the sea and the sea remains steady, so desires may enter a disciplined person without disturbing inner peace. The person who wants pleasures does not find peace.
verses.angle: The sea remains unmoving despite being filled
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is teaching Arjuna how to stay steady under pressure. Listen for the image he uses to show what inner peace looks like.

body.text: As rivers flow into the sea and the sea remains steady, so desires may enter a disciplined person without disturbing inner peace. The person who wants pleasures does not find peace. Listen to the sea, samudram, and the word describing it, acala-pratishtam, unmoving. The rivers of desire pour in, yet the sea does not swell; that is the steadiness Krishna offers. Krishna now states plainly that the person who gives up craving and ego is the one who attains peace.

verses.sa: विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः । निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति ॥
verses.tr: One who gives up all desires, moves without craving, without possessiveness, and without ego, attains peace.
verses.angle: Peace is for the one who acts without ego
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna describes the person who has found inner freedom. Listen to the three things this person leaves behind.

body.text: One who gives up all desires, moves without craving, without possessiveness, and without ego, attains peace. Three qualities are named in a row: without craving, without possessiveness, and without ego. The one who acts in this way is the one who attains peace. Krishna now names this state of freedom as the Brahmic state, the very state Arjuna must reach.

verses.sa: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति । स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna, this is the Brahmic state. Having reached it, one is never deluded. Remaining established in it even at the end of life, one attains freedom in the supreme reality.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna has just finished describing a mind at peace with itself. Now he gives this state a name, and with it a guarantee that even death cannot take it away.

body.text: Arjuna, this is the Brahmic state. Having reached it, one is never deluded. Remaining established in it even at the end of life, one attains freedom in the supreme reality. Krishna names the brahmic state: once reached, delusion ends, and even at death it holds. Arjuna now asks why Krishna urges him to fight if understanding is better than action.
